reason: The proof correctly applies the theorem that the inverse image of a closed set under a continuous function is closed; the singleton \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb R\).
text:
Since \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb R\), the inverse image \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). But
\[
f^{-1}(\{0\})=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=Z(f).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed.
